reconverted_2026_11_07.previous_converter: act_convert.py, the 2026-11-06 converter (kept outside the repository)
reconverted_2026_11_07.why: act_convert.py dropped every Word <w:sym> character with a code of F000 or more, which is how the register writes some characters in the Symbol and Wingdings fonts, and kept Symbol-font characters typed as text as raw private-use code points (U+F0xx), which display as empty boxes. act_convert_sym.py maps them to Unicode (Symbol F0D7 ·, F0B4 ×, F02D −, F0B7 •, F0A3 ≤, F0B3 ≥ and the like) and Wingdings boxes to "[ ]".
reconverted_2026_11_07.what_changed: Only bullets. 11 Symbol-font bullets kept as U+F0B7 (empty boxes) are written as "•": 2 in note 1 to schedule 1 principle 11 cl 7 (lines 796-797: what the new provider or new record keeper must do on a request for access) and 9 in note 1 to the dictionary, the list of terms defined by the Legislation Act (lines 872-880: adult to individual). Nothing had been dropped: no <w:sym> character is in the Word file, and no decimal point, multiplication sign, minus sign, inequality or tick box was lost. Reconverted from the same Word file (same sha256); the notice header is kept exactly and a diff against the first deposit shows no other change (same lines, same character and byte counts).
reconverted_2026_11_07.encodings_affected: none: baseline-2026-11 relies on no changed line (the two notes only point to ss 10, 12, 13-13D and to the Legislation Act dictionary; the encoding cites those provisions and principle 11 cl 7 directly, which the bullet glyph does not affect)
